note: Questions borrowed from a prediction market (Polymarket or Manifold) and resolved by it. The market price at selection is a benchmark, not part of our call; our forecasters did not look at it.

forecasts.rationale: The digest found no counted 2026 weekly series, only an NBC-reported 2025 pace of about 55 posts a day, roughly 390 a week (https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/elon-musk-s-x-activity-49-posts-on-politics-often-fringe/story, unchecked), so 180-199 (about 26-28 a day) would be a markedly quiet week for a window that spans the 2026 midterm aftermath. Weekly brackets listed for 2026 run from 80-99 to 500+ (https://explorer.struct.to/markets/elon-musk-of-tweets-november-7-november-14-140-159), so the distribution is wide and a 20-post bucket well below the recent pace holds only a small slice. Coherent with my 9% on the 320-339 bucket for Oct 30-Nov 6 (2026-11-02): that bucket sat near the middle of my expected range, and this one sits in the lower tail; evidence is thin and unchecked, so I keep some mass here rather than going lower.

questions.question: Will Elon Musk post 180-199 tweets from November 3 to November 10, 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the number of times Elon Musk (@elonmusk), posts on X from November 3 12:00 PM ET to November 10, 2026 12:00 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, only main feed posts, quote posts and reposts will count.

Replies will NOT count towards the total - however, replies on the main feed such as https://x.com/elonmusk/status/1786073478711353576 will be counted by the tracker.

Deleted posts will count as long as they remain available long enough to be captured by the tracker (~5 minutes).

Community reposts which are not counted by the tracker not count toward the total.

The resolution source for this market is the 'Post Counter' figure for posts found at https://xtracker.polymarket.com. Individual posts can be viewed by clicking "Export Data". If the tracker does not update correctly in accordance with the rules, X itself may be used as a secondary resolution source.
